info.name: MzaziCare API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the MzaziCare API, grouped so the folders can be run top to bottom.

Import this with the environment file beside it and choose that environment. Run **1. Sign in** first: it signs in every seeded account and saves their tokens, so every other request is already authorised. Tokens last 15 minutes; run it again when requests start answering 401.

Full guide: docs/api-testing.md

exec: pm.test('database and Redis are both up', () => {

item.name: 1. Sign in
item.description: Signs in each seeded account and saves its token to the environment. Run the whole folder before anything else, and again when requests start answering 401 (tokens last 15 minutes).

request.description: Any account with an email address can sign in with it instead of the phone number. The console offers this; the app does not.
Each refresh token works once. Running this twice with the same token signs the caregiver out everywhere, which is the replay protection working; run **Caregiver** sign-in again to recover.

item.name: Saying I'm here again changes nothing
2c. Answering by text
item.description:
Replying 1 or 2 to the alert SMS, as Africa's Talking would post it. Needs the API started with the same secret as the smsToken variable:

    SMS_INBOUND_TOKEN=local-text-replies-0123456789 npm run dev

Each reply's own answer is always 200, because the gateway resends anything else, so the effect is checked by reading the alert. The texts sent back appear in the API terminal, on lines starting [LoggingSmsProvider].

request.description: Mary, tier 1 for Grace, answers the alert text with 1. The API terminal shows the text sent back, with Grace's number and address.

item.name: It is Mary's now, answered by text

exec: pm.test('the trail says it came by text', () => pm.expect(taken.detail.via).to.eql('sms'));

request.description: A resend on a weak signal. Nothing changes; she is told she is already going.
Still 200, and nothing is sent back, so the address cannot be used to learn who is registered.

exec: pm.test('answers 404, as if the address did not exist', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

item.name: 2d. Talking through the app
item.description: A responder asks to talk, and the elder's alert then says who started. Needs a LiveKit project in backend/.env (LIVEKIT_URL, LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET; see running.md, Step 10). Without one, asking to talk answers 503 and that is checked instead. Postman only gets the token; joining the room is the app's job.

item.name: Mary asks to talk to Grace

request.description: A token for the emergency room, for the microphone only. Every join is audited.

exec: pm.test('answers 200, or 503 without a LiveKit project', () => pm.expect([200, 503]).to.include(pm.response.code));
pm.test('a token for this emergency room only', () => pm.expect(body.room).to.eql('emergency-' + pm.environment.get('alertId')));

item.name: Grace's alert says Mary started a call

exec: pm.test('not offered without a voice service', () => pm.expect(voice.available).to.eql(false));
pm.test('answers 403, or 503 without a LiveKit project', () => pm.expect([403, 503]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: 2g. Asking for help by text
item.description:
An elder with no data texting HELP to MzaziCare's shortcode, as Africa's Talking would post it. It raises the same alert the button does. Needs the API started with the same secret as 2c:

    SMS_INBOUND_TOKEN=local-text-replies-0123456789 npm run dev

Grace must have no alert open when it starts, or her text is answered with who is coming instead of raising one. The texts sent back appear in the API terminal, on lines starting [LoggingSmsProvider].

request.description: Grace has no data, so she texts HELP. The API terminal shows Mary being asked and Grace being told that the people who look after her have been told.

request.description: Only somebody asked at the current tier may decline.

4. Withdrawing and reopening
item.description: Run in order and quickly: an elder can only withdraw inside the 10 second grace window.

request.description: Refused with 409 after the grace window or once somebody has taken it on.
For a withdrawn alert nobody could confirm. The chain starts again.

item.name: Caregiver closes it with a note
5. Signing up
item.description: Needs one value you type yourself: the code. Send the first request, find the code in the terminal running the API (a line ending 'is your MzaziCare code'), put it in the environment's `code` variable, then send the second.

request.description: Always 202, whether or not a code was sent, so the endpoint cannot reveal who is registered. One code per number every 30 seconds.
role is CAREGIVER or FAMILY_MEMBER. A wrong or expired code answers 400. Each newPhone can sign up once; change it to sign up again.

item.description: Uses the account made in 5. Registering an elder needs a second code, sent to the elder's number.

request.description: Goes through the API to OpenStreetMap Nominatim, which allows one search a second for everybody. Do not run it in a loop. Saves the first match as the home for the next request.

request.description: No account for that number yet, so the place is held (status 'invited') until it signs up. Sending it twice answers 409, because a place is already held for that number. A different number is added beside it: everybody in the family rank is asked together.

exec: pm.test('their place is in the chain', () => pm.expect(held).to.be.an('object'));

item.name: 6b. Looking after an elder
item.description: Uses the elder registered in 6. Run after it.

request.description: careLevel null means 'not sure'. A home can be changed the same way: { "home": { latitude, longitude, label } }.
Refused with 409 while the elder has an emergency open, and with 400 for the caregiver's own place or a responder's.

item.name: 8b. My account
item.description: Uses the account made in 5, so the seeded accounts keep their password. The last request changes the password back.

request.description: Returns fresh tokens. Every other session for the account ends at its next refresh.

item.name: 8c. Forgotten password
item.description: Uses the account made in 5. Like signing up, it needs the code from the terminal running the API (a line ending 'password reset code'). Put it in the environment's `resetCode` variable before the second request. The new password is the same as the old one, so nothing else changes.

request.description: Always 202. A number with no account is sent nothing, and the answer is the same, so this cannot be used to learn who is registered.
